title: Rollout observability: cohort deltas, route-level metrics, and auto-rollback indicators
creator: Emily Chen
description:
Problem: Customers deploying new model versions need fast, actionable visibility into how canary/A-B/shadow rollouts affect per-route latency, token cost, and quality signals. Current Console exposes token counts and basic success rates but lacks (1) route-by-route cohort delta views, (2) end-to-end trace correlation with rollback triggers, and (3) an Auto-Rollback surface that explains why a rollback fired.

Background: Serving runtime emits per-request metadata including route, model_version, cohort_tag, latency_ms, tokens, and basic quality signals. ENG has an ingest pipeline (ENG-2789) that can emit 1m/5m aggregates; prior PM spikes (PM-4217, PM-5378) explored cohort delta UX but did not tie traces or rollback policy metadata into Console.

Proposal: Deliver a Console feature set with four pillars: (A) Cohort Delta Matrix - a sortable grid showing percent-delta and confidence indicators for metrics (latency P50/P95, median tokens, error rate, quality regression score) across routes; (B) Route Detail Timeline - cohort-filtered timelines that show SLO burn, traffic split, and sample request markers with links to distributed traces; (C) Auto-Rollback Dashboard - recent rollouts with the rule/policy that triggered rollback, first-detected delta, and quick actions (investigate, re-enable, annotate); (D) Differential Payloads API - thin read-only endpoint returning pre-aggregated cohort summaries for the UI within a 10s freshness SLA.

Scope: Backend cohort-aggregation and the Differential Payloads API, Console UI (Cohort Delta Matrix, Route Detail Timeline, Auto-Rollback Dashboard), significance-testing (bootstrap CI) for deltas, and trace linking.
Out of scope: full experiment lifecycle management, longitudinal archival analytics, and a separate feature flagging engine.

Tradeoffs: Pre-aggregating cohorts at ingest reduces frontend query costs but increases ingestion compute and storage. We will cap per-route cardinality (top N routes) for the MVP and expose sampling details in tooltips.

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged rollout to internal staging, follow with a 2-customer beta (one AI startup, one Enterprise SaaS), iterate, then gradual GA in console-2026.04.
acceptance_criteria: Console displays a Cohort Delta Matrix comparing two cohorts across routes and key metrics
Route detail page shows cohort-filtered timelines and links to representative distributed traces
Auto-Rollback dashboard lists recent rollouts with reason codes, rollback thresholds, and links to cohort deltas + traces
Differential Payloads API returns pre-aggregated cohort summaries within 10s for routes shown in the UI
All new Console surfaces are behind a feature flag and enabled for internal staging before beta
success_metrics: Median time-to-diagnose rollback cause reduced from 6h to <1h
>80% of rollbacks have an associated Console trace or link
At least 3 pilot customers mark cohort diffs as useful or highly useful
Incremental query cost for cohort deltas <= 20% over current Console backend budget
risks: Realtime aggregation cost could spike if naively materialized per-route per-cohort
UI complexity - too many metrics may overwhelm users; must prioritize and document
Private deployment customers may have data residency constraints that prevent cross-cohort joins
Rollback explanations may be noisy without signal conditioning and sample-size checks
